quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best way to stay close together while keeping enough space between riders?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets you stay close as a group while keeping safe space between riders. Use a single-file line when turning, in curves, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side with another rider.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, what should you do?

options.text: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you that you are downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed before shifting to a lower gear. Downshifting while going too fast can cause the motorcycle to jerk and the rear wheel to skid.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help protect you from serious injury?
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts out.

questions.question: What is true about brightly-colored helmets?

options.text: They may make it easier for the wearer to be seen.
They don't help improve a rider's visibility.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may make it easier for the wearer to be seen.
questions.explanation: A brightly-colored helmet is recommended. It protects you in a crash and helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: How should you brake on a motorcycle?

options.text: Only use the rear brake on slippery surfaces like wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help reduce your chance of a crash?

options.text: Be prepared to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible, clearly signal your intentions, keep a safe distance from other vehicles, and watch for hazards ahead. Do not rely on hoping other drivers see you.

questions.question: What should you do to control your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Increase your speed before entering the turn.
Look through the turn to see the best path.
Come to a complete stop before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to see the best path.
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle through a turn, look through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before turning and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: If you are riding next to another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay alongside the vehicle until the next exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in the vehicle's blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if danger appears. Either speed up or slow down to move away from the vehicle.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator discourage lane sharing by other drivers?

options.text: By giving dirty looks to other drivers
By riding in the center portion of the lane
By riding in the left portion of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane leaves less space on either side. This discourages other drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: A street-legal motorcycle must have all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a street-legal motorcycle must have: a rearview mirror, headlight with high and low beams, taillight, horn, muffler and tailpipe, brake light, front and rear brakes, and good tires. It must also be registered and have liability insurance. A flag is not required.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal usually located?
questions.explanation: The rear brake is controlled by a pedal near the right footrest.

questions.question: To increase your visibility, you should:

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, keep your headlight on all the time. Also wear brightly-colored or reflective clothing, and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
Ride a little faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: With a passenger, your motorcycle sits lower due to extra weight. Ride slower than usual, especially around curves and bumps. The extra weight means your motorcycle takes longer to speed up, slow down, and stop. Keep a larger space cushion between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: Riding in cold weather for long periods could cause all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Long rides in cold weather can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold. Hot flashes are not caused by cold weather riding.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, especially if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that other drivers see you, even if they look directly at you. Drivers often miss seeing motorcycles. Slow down when approaching intersections.

questions.question: Impairment from alcohol happens:
questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking any alcohol. Impairment begins well below the legal limit.

questions.question: To see better when preparing to pass a vehicle on its left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Try to stand up on your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane to see ahead better. This also makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Not signal your intentions, as that may distract the driver you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing. Signal your intentions and check for traffic. Pass only when it is safe, then signal and return to your lane.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery road, what should you do?

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to stay balanced.
Keep your speed the same to improve traction.
Don't worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: It is best to avoid slippery roads completely. If you cannot avoid a slippery area, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: What about riding between two vehicles moving in the same direction?

options.text: It is encouraged when traffic is heavy.
It is encouraged during the day to prevent traffic jams.
It is acceptable if the motorcyclist feels comfortable doing it.

questions.explanation: In Oregon, motorcycles and mopeds cannot pass between two moving vehicles on a multilane highway or one-way street. It is illegal.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help reduce your chances of a crash?

options.text: Be visible by wearing proper clothing and using your headlight.
Show your intentions by using turn signals and brake light.
Look for hazards in your path.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible to other drivers, show your intentions clearly, and keep space around your motorcycle. Look for and avoid hazards. Be ready to react to anything.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic on your left, where should you stay in your lane?

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Use your rearview mirrors more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay away from them. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. If traffic is coming toward you, stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead of you to see farther. Use your high beam headlight, except when you are near another vehicle.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: A pre-ride inspection should include tires, oil and fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn. Do a full pre-ride inspection before every ride.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions often to prevent boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around you.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around you.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly. The safest lane position also changes. Choose the position that gives you the most space and makes it easiest for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, a motorcycle operator should:

options.text: Always ride in the same part of the lane.
Change their lane position based on riding conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change their lane position based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best, and no position should always be avoided. Change your position based on the road and traffic conditions around you.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist stop other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Give dirty looks if another driver moves into your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill up the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When you want to stop drivers from trying to squeeze into your lane, ride in the center portion of the lane to discourage them.
